text:
Maya: heads up — hit a pretty rare crash in the page coordinator while running a noisy multi-tenant loadtest (heavy pin/unpin churn + async offload). attaching logs and minimal repro.
Aj: can you paste the stack trace and the exact repro script?
Maya: sure, gist below. error looks like an invalid page mapping after an eviction+remap race.
Maya: ```\n[2026-03-19T21:17:12Z] page-coord: claim failed: page=0x7f3b2c00 tid=2378 state=RESIDENT\n[2026-03-19T21:17:12Z] eviction: kick for tenant=42 slab=staging pool=HOST\n[2026-03-19T21:17:12Z] remap: remapping vaddr=0x7f3b2c00 -> hostpage=0x55f4c000\n[2026-03-19T21:17:12Z] fault: invalid mapping accessed by kernel\npanic: double-unmap detected\n```\n(repro script: loop pin/unpin 100k concurrently across 8 workers w/ batching enabled and prefetch=on)
Sasha: hmm this smells like a lifetime mismatch between the eviction token and the allocator's pin. maybe we allow `pin()` to succeed while eviction is concurrently clearing metadata.
Liam: yeah, we've seen similar in the segmented allocator where `evict()` races with `claim()` — usually a lost compare-and-swap on the page descriptor.
Aj: do we have telemetry for pin-latency / swap-window overlap? could be timing-specific.
Maya: telemetry shows a tight cluster of `pin_latency < 1ms` then an eviction burst right after; likely prefetch + async offload overlap.
Sasha: possible mitigation: introduce a short epoch handshake on pins — `pin(handle, epoch)` which refuses to pin if epoch < allocator_epoch. if eviction advances epoch after starting, pins fail fast and are retried.
Liam: that reduces races but also adds an API/ABI change. alternative: make `evict()` acquire a per-page exclusive stamp before removing mapping. but that hurts throughput for hot paths.
Aj: maybe a hybrid: fast-path optimistic pin (no syscall-like barrier), slow-path fallback that validates an epoch after pin before returning to caller. basically: try fast pin; if eviction flag seen, undo pin and go to slow path.
Maya: that sounds promising. slow path could block on `evict_quiesce()` which should be rare.
Sasha: also we need to ensure host fallback (when remap fails) doesn't double-free host pages. add refcount audit checks in debug builds and a soft-fail that logs instead of panic in canary.
Maya: I'll push a small debug build with extra refcount guards and epoch instrumentation to the staging pool. canary tag: `canary/page-race-debug-20260319`.
dev-bot: deploy queued: canary/page-race-debug-20260319 -> staging (8 GPUs), ETA 3m
Aj: once we have traces, we can decide between the epoch handshake vs optimistic-check. my vote is optimistic-check first since it's less invasive.
Liam: agreed. also add a unit test that fuzzes interleaving of `pin()`, `evict()`, and `remap()` using the allocator mock. we lack that coverage.
Sasha: and update the allocator API doc to call out "pin is not linearizable w.r.t eviction" until we land the fix so downstreams know the risk.
Maya: will do. I'll also create a short RFC follow-up proposing the optimistic-check patch and the epoch fallback design if the opt-check doesn't tame the repro. assigning follow-ups: Maya (debug deploy + logs), Aj (telemetry dash), Liam (fuzz test), Sasha (RFC draft).
Maya: thanks all — will post results when the canary finishes.

Maya: received, pulling logs now :eyes:
